land.text: Banten, the western port province of the Sunda Kingdom; the infobox lists the Sunda Kingdom, the Cirebon Sultanate and the Demak Sultanate as predecessors

predecessors.note: 'Syarif Hidayatullah conquered Banten: 1526' (infobox). Old Banten was a Cirebon-held province until the 1552 independence.

land.text: Old Banten, a province of Cirebon after 1531

predecessors.note: Independence from the Cirebon Sultanate in 1552 (infobox).

land.text: Banten, absorbed into the Dutch East Indies: 'The Sultanate of Banten had been absorbed into the territory of the Dutch East Indies', declared Daendels on 22 November 1808 in Serang

successors.note: Cliopatria's Dutch East Indies 1809 shape contains all 202 cells of the last Banten shape. The page's infobox says 'Annexed by the French Empire: 1808' and 'Annexed by the Dutch East Indies: 1813'; the article attributes 1808 to Daendels's administration; the sultan Muhammad Shafiuddin gave up the throne to Raffles in 1813.

capitals.name: Old Banten (Surosowan)
capitals.note: Infobox capital 'Old Banten'; the page gives no founding year for the capital. In 1808 Daendels ordered Aliyuddin II to 'move the capital to Anyer'; the sultan refused and Surosowan was destroyed. Coordinate from the gazetteer (Banten, 'Old Banten').

rulers.name: Maulana Hasanuddin
rulers.note: Infobox list. Syarif Hidayatullah (Sunan Gunung Jati) is listed as founder, 1552; Hasanuddin was crowned temenggong of Banten in 1531 under Cirebon.

rulers.name: Aliyuddin II
rulers.note: Exiled to Ambon after refusing Daendels in 1808. The infobox continues with caretaker Pangeran Suramenggala 1808-1809 and Muhammad Shafiuddin 1809-1813, after the dossier's end.

correction.text: Banten, conquered in 1526 and held as a Cirebon province until 1552

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1526-1528: 'Syarif Hidayatullah conquered Banten: 1526' (infobox), three years before Cliopatria's first Banten shape. Same 30-cell core as 1529, the Banten province. The infobox gives no area (only a 1696 population of 191,000 and a map caption for the 1570 extent), so no area ratio can be taken.

9,894 km2: the Banten coast and its pepper ports, 77 percent of Banten province. The page has Hasanuddin 'crowned temenggong of Banten' in 1531 under Cirebon and Banten independent in 1552. Applies 1529-1555.

Adds Lampung, south Sumatra and Bengkulu (62,964 km2). The pages give a span, not a year: Lampung 'brought under the reign of the Banten Sultanate by its first Islamic ruler, Maulana Hasanuddin (r. 1550-1570)' and at his death in 1570 the territory extended 'as far as Tulangbawang' and Bengkulu (Banten page). The 1556 year is Cliopatria's; unverified within the span. Applies 1556-1571.

Adds 65 cells of West Java (84,855 km2). The Sunda page has 'in the 1550s Hasanuddin, the sultan of Banten has launched a successful attack on Dayeuh Pakuan', the kingdom falling apart 'particularly after 1576 due to constant pressure from Banten', and razed 'by the Sultanate of Banten in 1579', after which Banten 'took over most of the former Sunda Kingdom's territory'. Cliopatria's 1572 year is inside that span; Cliopatria gives the east of the old Sunda shape (83 cells, West and Central Java) to Cirebon in 1579, where the page says 'most' went to Banten: left as drawn, flagged in notes. Applies 1572-1618.

Loses nine cells around Jayakarta (82,706 km2): Jayakarta was 'ruled by Prince Jayawikarta under the wider authority of the Banten Sultanate' and Coen 'overran Jayakarta' in May 1619, founding Batavia. Cliopatria's Dutch Republic 1620 shape takes 8 of the 9 cells. Applies 1619-1682.

Cliopatria takes 66 cells of West Java (Bogor, Priangan) from Banten in 1677 and gives them to its Dutch Republic row. The pages date the Dutch gain to the end of the civil war: 'The VOC gained Bogor and Priangan Highlands' after Ageng 'was forced to surrender' (Banten page; Ageng 'surrendered in March 1683', Ageng page; infobox 'Client state of VOC: 1683'), and the Ageng page has Banten gaining control of Cirebon and the Priangan highlands in the 1670s. So this shape holds 1683-1751, and the 1619 shape holds to 1682.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1807 shape without Lampung, south Sumatra and Bengkulu, annexed by the Dutch in 1752

keyframe_review.note: Lampung, south Sumatra and Bengkulu stay in Cliopatria's Banten shape to 1808, but 'The area was part of the Banten Sultanate until it was annexed by the Dutch in 1752' (Lampung page: renamed Residentie Lampoengse Districten) and 'In 1752 the Dutch annexed territories on western Borneo and southern Sumatra' (Banten page). From 1752 Banten is the Banten coast and its few West Java cells (about 15,000 km2). Applies 1752-1808; the Dutch East Indies 1809 shape contains all 202 cells, so Cliopatria's 1808 end leaves no gap.

region.text: Banten, conquered by Syarif Hidayatullah of Cirebon

ledger.note: 1526: Syarif Hidayatullah conquers Banten from the Sunda Kingdom. Infobox 'Syarif Hidayatullah conquered Banten: 1526'; in 1531 Hasanuddin was crowned temenggong of Banten and Old Banten became a Cirebon-held province (Banten page). Cliopatria starts the row in 1529.

region.text: Banten, no longer a Cirebon province

ledger.note: 1552: Banten becomes independent of Cirebon under Hasanuddin. Infobox 'Independence from Cirebon Sultanate: 1552'; the sultan list starts with Hasanuddin 1552-1570. In 1546 Hasanuddin left the kingdom to join Demak's Pasuruan campaign, after which Banten freed itself from Demak.

region.text: southern Sumatra 'as far as Tulangbawang' and Bengkulu: Lampung, part of South Sumatra and Bengkulu

ledger.note: 1556: Hasanuddin's rule reaches southern Sumatra. Hasanuddin gained control of southern Sumatra, and at his death in 1570 Banten's territory extended 'as far as Tulangbawang' and Bengkulu (Banten page); Lampung page: brought under Banten 'by its first Islamic ruler, Maulana Hasanuddin (r. 1550-1570)'. Page silent on the year: 1556 is Cliopatria's, inside the 1550-1570 span.

region.text: West Java: the parts of the Sunda Kingdom that Banten held from the attack on Dayeuh Pakuan

ledger.note: 1572: Banten holds the west of the old Sunda lands. The page has the attack on Dayeuh Pakuan 'in the 1550s', pressure 'particularly after 1576' and the razing in 1579; it gives no 1572. The year is Cliopatria's; Jayakarta/Sunda Kelapa, taken by Demak-backed forces in 1527, 'later came under the Banten Sultanate' (Jayakarta page, undated).

region.text: the remaining Sunda lands, Pakuan Pajajaran and the east of West Java

ledger.note: 1576: Banten's pressure on the Sunda Kingdom turns into the final campaign. 'The kingdom has fallen apart, particularly after 1576 due to constant pressure from Banten'.

1579: Banten razes Pakuan and the Sunda Kingdom ends. The Sunda Kingdom lasted 'until it was razed and destroyed by the Sultanate of Banten in 1579'; 'Thereafter, the Sultanate of Banten took over most of the former Sunda Kingdom's territory'. Cliopatria gives the 83 cells of the 1578 Sunda shape to Cirebon in 1579 and Banten no gain that year; left as drawn (notes).

region.text: Jayakarta, 'ruled by Prince Jayawikarta under the wider authority of the Banten Sultanate'

ledger.note: 1619: the Dutch storm Jayakarta and found Batavia. 'Dutch forces under Jan Pieterszoon Coen returned with reinforcements in May 1619, overran Jayakarta'; Banten page: Coen 'stormed and burnt Jayakarta to the ground', imposed 'a blockade of the Banten harbour, which went uninterrupted for some 15 years', and a 1639 treaty forced Banten to recognise Batavia.

1661: Banten extends its authority to Landak in western Borneo. 'In 1661, Banten extended authority to Landak in western Borneo' (Ageng page). Landak has no dossier and no gazetteer name; the circle is a guess around Ngabang.

region.text: Cirebon, whose princes Tirtayasa crowned as rival sultans at Banten

ledger.note: 1677: Ageng Tirtayasa makes himself master of Cirebon. In 1677 Tirtayasa had the Cirebon princes brought to Banten and crowned them as rival sultans, splitting Cirebon (Banten page); 'During the 1670s, Banten leveraged turmoil in the Mataram court to assert predominance over Cirebon' (Ageng page).

region.text: West Java, Bogor and the Priangan highlands, fought over by Banten and the VOC

ledger.note: 1680: open war with the VOC. 'Open war with the VOC began in 1680'; in May Haji confined Ageng in a palace coup and 'Ageng's faction was routed when VOC forces intervened for Haji' (Ageng page); Banten page: 'Civil war ensued for several years to come'.

1683: the VOC takes Bogor and the Priangan highlands and Banten becomes its client. 'The VOC gained Bogor and Priangan Highlands', and the Dutch demanded 'the expulsion of all foreigners from Banten, the Dutch monopoly on pepper trade' and a garrison (Fort Speelwijk). The page gives no year for the gain apart from the 1683 infobox; Cliopatria draws it in 1677. Banten's client status is the VOC dossier's vassal event, in the lighter tint (rule 4).

region.text: Cirebon and the Priangan highlands, over which Banten's predominance ended with Ageng's defeat

ledger.note: 1683: Banten's predominance over Cirebon ends with Ageng's surrender. Page silent on how Cirebon's relation ended; bridging reading of the 1683 defeat.

region.text: West Java, Bogor and the Priangan highlands

ledger.note: 1683: Ageng Tirtayasa surrenders to the VOC. 'Ageng surrendered in March 1683' (Ageng page); infobox 'Client state of VOC: 1683'.

region.text: Lampung, 'the area was part of the Banten Sultanate until it was annexed by the Dutch in 1752', and the rest of southern Sumatra

ledger.note: 1752: the Dutch annex Banten's lands in southern Sumatra. Lampung page: 'The area was part of the Banten Sultanate until it was annexed by the Dutch in 1752'; Banten page: 'In 1752 the Dutch annexed territories on western Borneo and southern Sumatra'. Cliopatria keeps them in Banten to 1808. Reviewer se-02-f: confidence lowered from 3 to 2. Both pages name Lampung and 'southern Sumatra' only; neither names Bengkulu or Sumatera Selatan for 1752 (the whole Sumatera Selatan admin1 also holds Palembang's core).

region.text: Landak in western Borneo, among the 'territories on western Borneo' annexed

ledger.note: 1752: the Dutch annex 'territories on western Borneo', which this dossier reads as including Landak. The page does not name Landak; bridging reading.

region.text: Banten, absorbed into the Dutch East Indies

ledger.note: 1808: Daendels abolishes the Sultanate of Banten. Aliyuddin II refused to 'move the capital to Anyer', Surosowan was destroyed and he was exiled to Ambon; 'The Sultanate of Banten had been absorbed into the territory of the Dutch East Indies', declared Daendels on 22 November 1808 in Serang. The page adds the sultanate 'ceased to exist' in 1813 when Raffles forced Muhammad Shafiuddin to give up his throne.

wars.name: Banten's conquest of the Sunda Kingdom

zones.text: Dayeuh Pakuan (Pakuan Pajajaran) and the Sunda lands

wars.outcome: Pakuan razed in 1579; the Sunda Kingdom ends and Banten 'took over most of the former Sunda Kingdom's territory'.
wars.note: The page says 'in the 1550s' for Hasanuddin's attack and 'particularly after 1576' for the decline; the ledger's contest runs 1576-1579.

wars.name: Banten-VOC conflict over Jayakarta and the pepper trade
wars.outcome: Jayakarta lost in 1619; a blockade of Banten harbour for about 15 years; a 1639 treaty forced Banten to recognise Batavia.
wars.note: The Jayakarta page gives May 1619 for the storming; the Dutch landed at Banten on 27 June 1596.

wars.name: Revolts of Bengkulu and Lampung
wars.outcome: 'Bengkulu rebelled in 1640 while Lampung rebelled in 1641 and 1644.' Both revolts were crushed.

wars.name: Pagarage (Pacirebonan) war
wars.outcome: A Banten victory over Cirebon-Mataram forces.

wars.name: Banten civil war and VOC intervention
wars.outcome: Haji, backed by the VOC, defeated his father Ageng Tirtayasa, who surrendered in March 1683; Banten became a VOC client state and the VOC gained Bogor and the Priangan highlands.
wars.note: The Banten page has Ageng storming the palace in 1682 after the death of Mangunjaya; the Ageng page dates open war to 1680.

certainty.note: No survey or treaty line anywhere: the Sumatran claim to 1752 is a sphere of ports and river mouths, and the West Java frontier moves with Mataram, Cirebon and the VOC without a dated line.

notes:
Five pages opened (budget 5). The Banten page gives no area; the Cliopatria areas could not be compared.
CLIOPATRIA ERRORS: (1) the Dutch gain of 66 West Java cells is drawn in 1677, the pages put it in 1683 (end of the civil war); (2) Lampung, south Sumatra and Bengkulu are kept in Banten to 1808 but the Dutch annexed them in 1752 (the Dutch Republic and Dutch East Indies shapes do not contain them in 1752-1808); (3) the 1526-1528 years are missing; (4) the Banten row ends 1808 (Daendels) while the sultan's line ends 1813.
FLAGGED, NOT CHANGED: the 83 cells of the Sunda Kingdom's last shape go to Cirebon in 1579 in Cliopatria but the Sunda page says Banten took 'most of the former Sunda Kingdom's territory' (Sumedang Larang inherited the regalia, undated); the Cirebon and Sunda dossiers should settle who holds the east. Landak (vassal 1661-1752) has no Cliopatria row. Banten as VOC client state 1683-1808 is for the Dutch Republic dossier (eu-09) as vassal_start/vassal_end with counterpart sultanate-of-banten.
PAGE SILENT: the date of Banten's Lampung conquest inside 1550-1570; when Sunda Kelapa passed from Demak/Cirebon to Banten; the 1659 treaty terms; the 1682/1684 Cisadane line; Bengkulu's status under the British ('Western coastal regions beyond the Barisan Mountains' of Lampung were British Bencoolen from the 1680s to 1824).
Gazetteer: Landak, Ngabang, Tulangbawang, Priangan and Dayeuh Pakuan are not in regions/places (Bogor is a place).
